openClinicalQuestions: Clinician review of escalation wording: acutely painful, firm lump that will not reduce, especially with vomiting → urgent care for possible strangulated hernia—confirm preferred patient-facing phrasing for Indian emergency pathways.

claimLedger.claim: Defines DRAM as rectus halves moving apart with pregnancy stretch; lists doming, gap feeling, discomfort; advises graded core work and physio referral.
claimLedger.sourceSection: POGP · Tummy muscle separation (DRAM) in pregnancy · not stated
claimLedger.limitations: UK patient leaflet; symptom lists are not diagnostic criteria

claimLedger.claim: Hernia is organ/tissue through muscle gap; pain around hernia with nausea/vomiting warrants urgent advice pathway.
claimLedger.sourceSection: NHS · Hernia · not stated on fetched page
claimLedger.limitations: General hernia overview; not specific to postpartum diastasis

claimLedger.claim: Strangulated hernia (blocked blood supply) is a medical emergency; call emergency services for severe pain, vomiting, colour change, inability to pass wind/stool.
claimLedger.sourceSection: NHS · Umbilical hernia · Page last reviewed 24 November 2025
claimLedger.limitations: Umbilical-hernia page; apply carefully when counselling midline lumps
